newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Red Cross takes Mrs Karadzic's complaint to NATO.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross takes Mrs Karadzic's complaint to NATO.

text.p: The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) said it asked NATO on Friday to look into allegations by the wife of Radovan Karadzic that NATO troops misused the Red Cross symbol while arresting a war crimes suspect in Bosnian Serb territory.

Ljiljana Karadzic, head of the Red Cross in Bosnian Serb territory, wrote to ICRC chief Cornelio Sommaruga alleging that NATO soldiers had entered the Prijedor hospital on Thursday carrying a Red Cross parcel and pretending to deliver medicine.

Their mission was to arrest Milan Kovacevic, director of the hospital in the northwest town of Prijedor, charged by the U.N. war crimes tribunal in connection with a genocidal campaign to deport Moslems and Croats in 1992 at the start of the conflict.

"The letter alleges that a Red Cross parcel was used as a pretext in the arrest of Milan Kovacevic," ICRC spokeswoman Amanda Williamson told Reuters in Geneva. "We take the allegations very seriously, of course.
"But we need to establish now exactly what happened yesterday. Today we have taken up contacts with NATO... to find out exactly what happened."

The letter from Ljiljana Karadzic -- whose husband has been indicted twice by the Hague tribunal and remains at large -- asks the ICRC to condemn the use of the parcel with the symbol of the red cross on white background, according to Williamson.
The Geneva-based humanitarian organisation, which helps victims of war, expected to issue a statement later in the day.

The Bosnian Serb Red Cross is not one of the 171 national societies recognised by the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC), also based in Geneva. The two umbrella groups form the International Red Cross Movement.
